quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if clothes are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good clothing can reduce injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. They should be made of sturdy material and fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.

questions.question: Waiting one hour after having one drink before you ride:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Means your riding skills will not be affected.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.
May not fully remove alcohol from your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not fully remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Your body can get rid of about one drink per hour. But the time needed varies from person to person. It is safest not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: You should do a complete check of your motorcycle:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
Side effects may still be present.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body can get rid of about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is the most important piece of equipment a rider must wear?
questions.correctAnswerText: A helmet
questions.explanation: A helmet is the most important safety equipment a rider can wear. One in five motorcycle crashes causes head and neck injuries. A helmet can greatly improve your chances of survival.

questions.question: Your best source of information about your motorcycle is:
questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual has the most accurate information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how to operate it and how to maintain it.

questions.question: A motorcycle needs:

options.text: Less frequent checks than a car.
More frequent checks than a car.
Pre-ride checks only by a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent checks than a car.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than a small problem on a car. Check your motorcycle more often. Do a complete check before every ride.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for a motorcycle operator?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced boots are best, or high-top boots and heavy shoes work well. If your shoes have long laces, tuck them away before riding.

questions.question: The best source of information for your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who has a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It will help you understand your specific model.

questions.question: When buying a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Items made of leather.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket that cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the highest level of protection.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps other drivers see you in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothing during the day too.

questions.question: What is an advantage of wearing gloves?

options.text: They make it easier to control the motorcycle.
They help other drivers identify you.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: What should protective motorcycle pants be like?

options.text: Loose enough to flap in the wind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make gestures.
Speed up to increase distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you faster and increase danger.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: It is too dangerous for inexperienced riders.
Use it to occasionally help the rear brake.
Use it together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why are mirror checks important?

options.text: Use them only on long trips.
They should be part of your regular scanning routine.
They don't help because you can't control what's behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly as part of your normal routine. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What should you consider when choosing a lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
Which position makes your trip shorter.
Which position lets you pass more vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes sure other drivers can see you and gives you enough space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which helmet gives you the most protection?

options.text: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
One that has survived a previous crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that meets U.S. DOT standards.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all around your head.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.correctAnswerText: By downshifting.
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a common way to slow down. Remember that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see you?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen better, wear bright clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle or uneven surface, approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off your seat so your knees can absorb some impact. Just before contact, roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling often means a tire has failed. If your motorcycle feels different while riding, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What can reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator. They should hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Boots that go over the ankle
A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Turn signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are not very important because motorcycles are small.
Are very important for alerting other drivers to your plans.
Should only be used when other vehicles are nearby.
Are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are very important for alerting other drivers to your plans.
questions.explanation: As a motorcycle rider, you are at greater risk. Always use turn signals to alert others to your plans. Use them every time you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
Lets you rely on others to spot hazards.
Requires you to ride faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle on all sides gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: To prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface, a motorcyclist should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce their speed.
questions.explanation: When riding on a slippery surface, decrease your speed. Sudden moves on a slippery surface can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Ride it like your own bike since all bikes are basically the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is slightly different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle. Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: When you take alcohol and drugs together, the effects are:

options.text: Stronger than when you take either one alone.
Less dangerous than when you take either one alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stronger than when you take either one alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can hurt your ability to ride safely. Some drugs become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: Oil in the center of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers in the road are more dangerous for a motorcycle than dry pavement.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of an accident, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show what you plan to do. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should choose shoes with soles that:

options.text: Are hard, tough, and do not slip.
Allow air to reach your feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are hard, tough, and do not slip.
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Pick shoes with soles made of hard, durable material that does not slip.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when you ride. Good protective gear includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: Riding gloves are often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: When you brake, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time to stop. The brakes work best when you use them together.

questions.question: To get the best protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.correctAnswerText: U.S. Department of Transportation.
questions.explanation: For the best protection, use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Do not protect your eyes as well as eyeglasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes, but only a face shield protects your whole face. Eyeglasses are not good enough to replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to keep your balance.
Keep your speed the same to improve grip.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as possible.
questions.explanation: The best choice is to avoid slippery roads entirely. If you cannot avoid a slippery area, keep your motorcycle straight and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Pick one spot in the lane and always stay there.
Weave back and forth across the lane to prevent other drivers from sharing it.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where you position yourself in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position in the lane as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Keep other drivers from using your lane.
Give you a nice view of the scenery.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide what you plan to do from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from using your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps with safety in many ways. It keeps you out of other vehicles' blind spots, helps you see and be seen better, helps you avoid road hazards, protects you from wind from other vehicles, and gives you a way to escape dangers. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from drinking.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from drinking.
questions.explanation: The body breaks down about one drink per hour on average. However, alcohol can build up in your body. Your ability and judgment can still be impaired even if you wait.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You do not need to look over your shoulder if you check your mirrors.
Your mirrors show you everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume other drivers will see your turn signal and respond correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Alcohol impairment:

options.text: Starts at about half the legal limit.
Only happens at the legal limit.
Only happens if you have had multiple drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Starts with the first drink.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired below the legal limit. No amount of alcohol is safe before riding.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, the operator should:

options.text: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
Deflate the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not tell passengers about upcoming hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger's weight. Keep a bigger space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen to:

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new, untrained riders who are not familiar with their motorcycle.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.
